title.narrative: Activity under preparation Top up EUROFRONT

description.narrative: The overall objective of the proposed action is to contribute to security, improved respect for and protection of human rights, and social and economic development at national and regional levels in Latin America, through the strengthening of Integrated Border Management (IBM) and support to the fight against human trafficking and the smuggling of migrants. The action will be structured around two main components. On the one hand, it seeks to increase the effectiveness and efficiency of border management at four key land border crossing points and eventually any other in the best strategic interest in the region by introducing advanced elements of IBM. On the other hand, it aims to support regional mechanisms for safe human mobility and the fight against human trafficking and migrant smuggling, by reinforcing ans expanding the action of existing operational networks for document verification (such as Point Athens) and migration intelligence, as well as integrating customs security actions that ensure legitimate trade flows and enable effective border control to combat transnational crime. The action will also support regional initiatives such as the MERCOSUR Linked Border Localities, the Border Integration Zones (ZIFs), and the Andean Data Bank of the Andean Community of Nations (CAN), in order to strengthen a coordinated and comprehensive approach to mobility and security. Cooperation with relevant EU agencies and Member State counterparts will be fostered. A significant capacity development process will also be supported through different strategies and methodologies, with a strong orientation towards supporting partner countries in the preparation and implementation of a national border management strategy and action plan. Adopting a ¿variable geometry focus,¿ which acknowledges the political and geostrategic diversity among Latin American countries, the programme will concentrate on selected geographical areas and specific borders located in South America. In this sense, it is designed to act as a catalyst within the region¿s diverse regional and sub-regional integration processes (e.g., MERCOSUR) and existing bilateral cooperation frameworks for addressing IBM-related challenges. Aligned with the 2030 Agenda and the European Consensus on Development, this initiative also contributes to the EU-LAC Partnership on Justice and Security.
